rationale: The pattern P-LIT-PRIORITIZE suggests reordering tests to provide earlier failure feedback. In a Go environment, running 'go test -short' or specific high-value packages first can achieve this. However, since the exact failure-prone tests are unknown without historical data, a common prioritization strategy is to run tests with the '-race' flag or specific sub-packages. Since I must preserve all original commands and cannot determine the best test order without history, I will implement a minimal change that separates the test execution into two stages: a fast/short test run followed by the full test suite. This follows the 'Rank tests' mechanism by attempting to surface failures earlier in the pipeline. I will also add caching for Go dependencies to ensure the baseline performance is not degraded by the split.
